name: Fiji
headline: Fiji: +2.5% growth in 2025, −1.4% inflation, debt 77% of GDP
sections: Fiji is a $6.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 170th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $16K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 9.1% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose −1.4% in 2025, in deflation, down from 6.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.0% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 15.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 77% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has risen from 66% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.4% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −7.7% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 119% of GDP (2024), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 4.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 87% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 67.5 years (2024). Population: 928 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
